# A childless element call is the same node whichever way its tag is spelled.
#
# `text #row(…)` and `ui.text #row(…)` are one node written twice, and they
# generated different pages. The checker's CallStmt arm resolves the callee
# itself -- bare ident, `ns.Field` declared, `ns.Field` through a wildcard --
# and then the branch that handles an `#id` threw that answer away and redid
# it with a bare `c.scope.Lookup(name)`. A namespaced member is not a scope
# name, so the qualified spelling came out with a nil Component and
# `Name: "ui.text"`:
#
#   - no declaration, so no prop defaults -- the style binding below is
#     emitted for one spelling and not the other;
#   - not an element call at all as far as elementRefCallInfo was concerned,
#     so declareNodeIDs bound no handle and a handler naming `#row` was
#     `undefined: row` under an aliased import and fine under a dot import;
#   - `ui.text` reaching a platform, which android refuses with
#     `no composable for component "ui.text"`.
#
# cmpgen rather than a grep, because the claim is that the two pages are the
# same page and no single assertion says that.

sngl generate --platform html -o out-qualified qualified.sngl
sngl generate --platform html -o out-dot dot.sngl
cmpgen out-qualified/index.html out-dot/index.html

-- qualified.sngl --
import ui "sngl:ui"

output {
    none {
        html
    }
}

ui.window #w(title="t") {
    ui.text #row(value="a")

    ui.button(text="go", @click {
        row.value = "x"
    })
}

-- dot.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"

output {
    none {
        html
    }
}

window #w(title="t") {
    text #row(value="a")

    button(text="go", @click {
        row.value = "x"
    })
}
